title: Frobenius and Verschiebung on affine commutative groups
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] of characteristic $p>0$, and let $G$ be a commutative affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $C=k[G]$ with coordinate Hopf maps $\Delta,\epsilon,S$ [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf], and put $\sigma(c)=c^p$, $C^{(p)}=C\otimes_{k,\sigma}k$, $G^{(p)}=\operatorname{Spec}C^{(p)}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with the base-changed group operations. Tensor products are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Relative Frobenius is the group homomorphism $F_G:G\to G^{(p)}$ with coordinate map $f_C:C^{(p)}\to C$, $a\otimes c\mapsto ca^p$. There is a canonical group homomorphism $V_G:G^{(p)}\to G$, defined by the following construction on coordinates. Let $\Delta_p:C\to C^{\otimes p}$ be iterated comultiplication, and let $\mathfrak S_p$ act by permuting tensor factors. Choose any $k$-basis $B$ of $C$. The invariant space $(C^{\otimes p})^{\mathfrak S_p}$ has a basis consisting of the sums of the distinct basis tensors in each permutation orbit. Define $\lambda_C:(C^{\otimes p})^{\mathfrak S_p}\to C^{(p)}$ by sending the singleton orbit $b^{\otimes p}$ to $b\otimes1$ and every non-singleton orbit sum to zero. This map is independent of $B$; the image of $\Delta_p$ is invariant, and $v_C=\lambda_C\Delta_p:C\to C^{(p)}$ is a Hopf algebra homomorphism, in the sense of a $k$-algebra map preserving comultiplication, counit and antipode [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor], defining $V_G$. These maps satisfy $V_G\circ F_G=[p]_G$, where $[p]_G$ sums $p$ copies on every algebra-valued point. No connectedness or perfection hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Definition 11.39 and Proposition 11.40(a), printed pp.224-225. The basis-orbit description spells out the canonical linear map in the diagram of Definition 11.39.

proof.text: Use the coordinate Hopf maps of [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. Commutativity of the group law in [def-sc-group-scheme] gives $s\Delta=\Delta$ by pulling back $m\circ s=m$. Coassociativity gives all bracketings of $\Delta_p$ the same value. Swapping any adjacent outputs is then insertion of $s\Delta=\Delta$ into that iterated map, so $\Delta_p(C)\subset I_p(C)$. Iterating the algebra-map identity for $\Delta$ also gives $\Delta_p(ab)=\Delta_p(a)\Delta_p(b)$ and $\Delta_p(1)=1^{\otimes p}$.

source.place: Section 11(i), printed p.224, comultiplication into invariant tensors

proof.text: The Frobenius map is well-defined: $(ra)\otimes c=a\otimes r^pc$ has the same image $cr^pa^p$. The binomial expansion gives $(a+b)^p=a^p+b^p$, since $p$ divides every intermediate binomial coefficient; products and units are preserved directly. Thus $f_C(a\otimes c)=ca^p$ is a $k$-algebra map. Scalar extension [def-weil-module-base-change] and the tensor multiplication [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] give, for $\Delta(a)=\sum a_i\otimes b_i$, $(f_C\otimes f_C)\Delta^{(p)}(a\otimes c)=c\sum a_i^p\otimes b_i^p=\Delta(ca^p)$. Likewise $\epsilon f_C(a\otimes c)=c\epsilon(a)^p=\epsilon^{(p)}(a\otimes c)$ and $S f_C=f_C S^{(p)}$. Hence the spectrum functor gives the stated group homomorphism $F_G$.

source.place: Section 11(i), printed p.224, Frobenius coordinate map and reference to 2.28

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-symmetric-invariant-frobenius-projection] with $M=C$. It gives exactly the orbit basis, basis-independent map $\lambda_C$, naturality, and tensor compatibility required here. Define $v=\lambda_C\Delta_p$. For invariant $x,y$, apply naturality to $\mu:C\otimes C\to C$ and then tensor compatibility: $\lambda_C(xy)=\mu^{(p)}\kappa(\lambda_C(x)\otimes\lambda_C(y))=\lambda_C(x)\lambda_C(y)$. With $x=\Delta_p(a),y=\Delta_p(b)$, step 1 implies $v(ab)=v(a)v(b)$. Naturality for $k\to C$ and the unit clause give $v(1)=1$ and $v(r)=1\otimes r$. Thus $v$ is a $k$-algebra map.

source.place: Definition 11.39, printed p.224, the invariant-tensor arrow and coordinate homomorphism

proof.text:
Write $\tau$ for interleaving two blocks of $p$ factors. The Hopf identities give
$$\Delta^{\otimes p}\Delta_p=\tau(\Delta_p\otimes\Delta_p)\Delta.$$
Indeed both sides are $2p$-fold iterated comultiplication: coassociativity removes brackets and cocommutativity, as in step 1, allows the interleaving permutation. Apply naturality of $\lambda$ to $\Delta:C\to C\otimes C$, then its tensor formula to the right-hand side. Under $\kappa$ this yields $\Delta^{(p)}v=(v\otimes v)\Delta$. Applying naturality to $\epsilon$ and $S$ similarly gives $\epsilon^{(p)}v=\epsilon$ and $S^{(p)}v=vS$: the input identities are $\epsilon^{\otimes p}\Delta_p(a)=\epsilon(a)1^{\otimes p}$ (iterate the counit identity), and $S^{\otimes p}\Delta_p=\Delta_pS$ (pull back the elementary group identity $(g_1\cdots g_p)^{-1}=g_1^{-1}\cdots g_p^{-1}$ in a commutative group). Thus $v$ preserves all three Hopf maps. By [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor], it defines the canonical group homomorphism $V_G$.

source.place: Definition 11.39 and its functoriality/product properties, printed pp.224-225

proof.text: Let $\mu_p:C^{\otimes p}\to C$ multiply the factors. For a singleton orbit $b^{\otimes p}$, both $f_C\lambda_C$ and $\mu_p$ give $b^p$. For a nonconstant orbit with multiplicities $n_1,\ldots,n_r<p$ summing to $p$, its size is $p!/(n_1!\cdots n_r!)$, divisible by $p$ because the denominator is prime to $p$. All its tensors have the same product. Consequently $\mu_p(s_O)=0=f_C\lambda_C(s_O)$. The orbit basis gives $f_C\lambda_C=\mu_p$ on $I_p(C)$, hence $f_Cv=\mu_p\Delta_p$. On $R$-points the last map sends $a$ to the value of $a$ on the product of $p$ copies of that point, by the definition of the coordinate comultiplication. It is therefore the pullback of $[p]_G$. Contravariance of spectrum identifies $f_Cv$ with $V_G\circ F_G$, proving the identity. No cancellation of Frobenius, reducedness, connectedness or inverse of $\sigma$ was used.

source.place: Proposition 11.40(a), printed p.225, commuting coordinate square
